usageNotes: Creates a VNC shell proxy for direct node-level console access — use this for host OS access rather than VM/container console (which have their own vncproxy endpoints). The caller must hold Sys.Console on /nodes/{node}; the special-purpose commands 'ceph_install' and 'upgrade' additionally require root@pam authentication — API tokens cannot satisfy that requirement. Returns connection credentials (ticket, cert, port) consumed immediately by a VNC or noVNC websocket client; the session is ephemeral and the ticket expires quickly, so the client should connect without delay.

examples.summary: Open a standard login shell on node pve01 via websocket

tips: The returned 'ticket' and 'password' fields are used as VNC credentials; pass 'ticket' as the VNC password when connecting via the standard VNC protocol path.
Set 'websocket: true' for noVNC browser clients — the Proxmox web UI always uses websocket mode.
The 'cmd-opts' field is null-byte delimited, not space delimited; construct it carefully if passing arguments to 'upgrade' or 'ceph_install'.
Width and height are cosmetic hints to the spawned terminal; the VNC client can resize after connection.
